title: asq Office operation
description: The 202 body of every changed 1.4 mutation and the 200 body of GET /api/operations/{id} (backend-v1.4.md §4, §6). A 200 on a mutation is a Receipt — the work finished and receipt.json describes what happened. A 202 is this: the work is owned by the back-end beyond the request, and the client polls. A v1.3 client cannot receive one, because every route that can answer 202 requires the X-Office-Contract: 1.4 handshake first.

operation_id.description: Opaque, server-generated, stable for the life of the operation. Never the Idempotency-Key: the key is the client's, this is the back-end's.

receipt.description: The Receipt the work produced, once it produced one. Null for every status but succeeded — in particular outcome_unknown never carries a receipt, because inventing one would claim delivery the back-end did not observe.

error.description: Null unless status is failed or outcome_unknown. A local 4xx/5xx that never became an operation is error.json instead; backend-v1.4.md §7 documents the translation.

OperationStatus.description: outcome_unknown is not success and is not failure: the back-end delivered something it could not confirm, so it will not be retried automatically and the client must not present it as done. Only succeeded carries a receipt.

OperationKind.description: Finite: exactly the changed 1.4 mutations of backend-v1.4.md §4. A retained legacy mutation never produces an Operation, so no kind exists for one.

OperationTarget.title: OperationTarget
OperationTarget.description: Only local identifiers the server resolved itself. Never a pane id, a tmux target, a filesystem path, a workspace key, a credential reference or any part of the validated body — the browser learns nothing from a target it did not already name.
